answer: Passport-chip check: an identity taps the NFC chip in a passport, whose data the issuing country signs. A verifier checks that signature against the published country certificate list and derives a one-way nullifier from the document number, so one passport cannot back two active identities. A sonnet-writing farm of bots gains nothing without more genuine passports, which are costly and illegal to obtain; a forged ivory booklet with no valid chip fails. Limits: stolen passports still pass, people without one are excluded, and if the cipher behind nullifiers leaks, holders can be tracked.
